messages:
Emma Clarke: Heads-up — BlueForge sent the weekly pricing feed and there are three surprises in the CSV. can someone from cost-modeling pick this up? :eyes:
Javier Ruiz: I can take a look. any docs on their new 'commit_fraction' field?
BlueForge-bot: Automated feed uploaded: s3://bf-pricing/feeds/2024-11-05/blueforge_feed_q4.csv (md5: a1b2c3). Fields: region, sku_id, list_price_usd, reserved_price_usd, spot_price_usd, commit_fraction, eviction_window_minutes, billing_key
Sophie Patel: The weird part is commit_fraction is 0-100 but they sometimes include decimals like 12.5. our parser expects integers for buckets.
Liam Chen: That will break the reserved allocation step in the cost sim. we need to normalize to a float and then map to our commit buckets.
Emma Clarke: Action: Javier -> normalize feed + explain any assumptions. Sophie -> check billing_key mapping. I will ping BlueForge PM about eviction window semantics.
Javier Ruiz: Quick question — for rows where reserved_price_usd is empty but commit_fraction > 0, should we treat as "price TBA" or infer from list_price * (1 - commit_fraction/100)?
Sophie Patel: Don't infer. flag as vendor-missing-price. we should surface to partners for correction. Add a delta column in the normalized output for modeling.
BlueForge-bot: Note: some SKUs have region code 'eu-central-1a' (availability zone) instead of just 'eu-central-1'.
Liam Chen: Normalize region to AZ-level vs region-level is important. Our downstream billing_key aggregation is region-based, otherwise we double-count.
Emma Clarke: Sophie — map their billing_key -> our billing_key table and list any unmatched keys. include suggested fallback rules.
Sophie Patel: Will do. also found preempt_penalty column on a few lines (not documented). sending sample rows in a follow-up.
Javier Ruiz: Prototype normalizer (ran locally):
```
# pseudocode
for row in feed:
  row.commit_fraction = float(row.commit_fraction)
  row.region = row.region.split('-a')[0] if row.region.endswith(tuple('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz')) else row.region
  if row.reserved_price_usd == '':
    row.price_status = 'vendor-missing-price'
```
Javier Ruiz: Output CSV columns: billing_key, vendor_sku, region, list_price_usd, reserved_price_usd, spot_price_usd, commit_fraction_norm, price_status, source_md5
Emma Clarke: Nice. Please commit normalizer to partnerships drive and ping partners-ops when ready. Include a small sample of 10 rows and an unexpected-value summary.
partners-ops: noted. I'll coordinate a quick vendor QA call if BlueForge doesn't supply corrected rows by EOD tomorrow.
Sophie Patel: FYI — invoice alignment: BlueForge invoices per billing_key-month; they may aggregate AZ SKUs under one billing_key. we need mapping rules to avoid double-billing in our cost model.
Liam Chen: Also add a flag for eviction_window_minutes > 120 — treat as effectively non-preemptible for scheduling heuristics.
Emma Clarke: Good call. Javier, add that rule in the normalizer and add a short README in the repo explaining edge cases.
Javier Ruiz: On it. ETA 6pm PT today. I'll attach normalized sample and the bad-rows list to the thread when done.
BlueForge-bot: Follow-up from BlueForge: PM says commit_fraction is target average reserve utilization across a month, decimals expected. will send updated CSV with integer commit_bucket by end of day.
Emma Clarke: Thanks. if they do that, we still need to keep decimals in the model for smoothing, but map to integer buckets only for billing_key rollups.
Sophie Patel: I'll prepare a small mapping table: decimal->bucket rule + rationale for finance.
partners-ops: scheduling vendor QA 11:30am PT tomorrow. invite sent to blueforge-pm, blueforge-ops, finance-ops, eng-cost.
Emma Clarke: Perfect. closing loop: deliverables — normalized feed (Javier), billing_key mapping + unmatched list (Sophie), vendor QA call (partners-ops). :thumbsup:
